chain.actions: LEFT or RIGHT; both legal before termination.
chain.transitions: RIGHT increases position by 1; LEFT decreases it by 1, bounded at 0.
chain.reward: -1 per transition, except arrival at 2 gives +5.
chain.boundary: Arrival at 2 is true termination. A separate 6-step wrapper demonstrates external truncation; underlying chain continues.
chain.randomness: Deterministic dynamics; optionally seeded random action choices.

switch.state: Hidden mode bit 0/1 and whether an action has finished the episode.
switch.observation: Broken observation is constant 0; repaired observation includes mode.
switch.transitions: FLIP toggles mode; CLAIM terminates without changing mode.
switch.reward: FLIP gives 0; CLAIM gives +1 in mode 1, -1 in mode 0.
switch.boundary: CLAIM terminates; optional external collection cap truncates.
switch.randomness: Reset mode sampled uniformly with an explicit seed; witness traces set mode directly.

trajectory.boundary: Terminate after all three rewards; no bootstrap.

branch.state: A (start), B, T (terminal); finite-horizon extension includes decisions remaining.
branch.observation: Full state; remaining decisions in the horizon extension.
branch.actions: At A: DIRECT or VIA; at B: FINISH. No terminal actions.
branch.transitions: DIRECT: A->T; VIA: A->B; FINISH: B->T.
branch.boundary: At most two decisions, then true termination.
branch.randomness: None; fixed-policy evaluation uses a 50/50 choice at A.

lottery.state: Start S and terminal outcomes WIN/LOSS/SAFE.
lottery.transitions: SAFE->SAFE surely; RISKY->WIN with p=0.25, otherwise LOSS.
lottery.randomness: Bernoulli outcome, seeded; widget computes exact expectation.

weather.actions: State evolves independently; one-step decision extension chooses UMBRELLA or NONE before next regime.
weather.reward: Chain alone gives 0; decision extension gives 1 for matching UMBRELLA to WET or NONE to DRY, else 0.
weather.boundary: Chain is continuing, sample length truncates; extension is one-step terminal.

td.state: S, successor N, terminal T; transitions supplied as a fixed batch.
td.actions: At N three stored action values [4,8,99], with mask [true,true,false].
td.transitions: Witness supplies S->N with reward 1, or S->T with reward 1.
td.reward: Specified sample reward, not an assumed training distribution.
td.boundary: T terminal; separate N time-limit truncation retains bootstrap.

bandit.state: One start state and terminal after action.
bandit.actions: A or B; optional third masked action C.
bandit.transitions: Each action ends one episode; reset starts a new independent draw.
bandit.reward: A yields Bernoulli(0.4), B Bernoulli(0.8); C is illegal.
bandit.randomness: Seeded rewards and independent seeded behaviour policy. Gradient witnesses supply reward explicitly.

shortcut.actions: START: shortcut or detour; RISK: careful or slip; SAFE: finish.
shortcut.transitions: START shortcut->RISK, detour->SAFE; all subsequent actions->T.
shortcut.randomness: Environment deterministic; epsilon-greedy chooses RISK actions.

bins.state: One decision with continuous x in [0,1].
bins.observation: Exact x; broken encoder merges values 0.49 and 0.51.
bins.reward: LEFT=1 if x<0.5, else 0; RIGHT=1 if x>=0.5, else 0.
bins.randomness: Training x sampled uniformly with seed; deterministic witnesses use boundary values.

regression.state: Teaching dataset, not an interacting environment: x in [0,1].
regression.actions: Two output coordinates representing action values.
regression.transitions: No environment transitions; supervised warm-up before DQN.
regression.reward: Known labels Q(x)=[x,1-x]; no reward sampling.
regression.boundary: Fixed optimizer-step budget; not an RL episode.
regression.randomness: Seeded initialization; exact forward/gradient witnesses use fixed parameters.

replay.state: Four-state chain and a FIFO buffer of transitions.
replay.observation: Position plus action mask; inspectable buffer and separate online/target parameters.
replay.actions: ADVANCE or RESET at nonterminal positions.
replay.transitions: ADVANCE progresses 0->1->2->3; RESET returns to 0. Buffer capacity 4.
replay.boundary: 3 terminates; cap collection at 8 steps with truncation.
replay.randomness: Seeded uniform sampling with replacement from stored transitions.

double.state: Fixed transition S->N and inspectable online/target outputs.
double.observation: Batch of supplied states with next-action masks.
double.transitions: No sampled dynamics needed; target calculation consumes fixed transition.
double.randomness: None; optional noisy-estimate illustration is seeded and labelled illustrative.

priorities.state: Replay entries i=0,1,2 with raw priorities [1,4,9].
priorities.observation: Priority, sampling probability, and importance weight per item.
priorities.actions: Sample a replay index; no environment actions.
priorities.transitions: Update raw priority after observing TD error; FIFO replacement stage.
priorities.reward: No environment reward; witness squared TD losses [1,4,9].
priorities.boundary: Fixed number of sample/update operations, not an episode.

team.state: Ready or terminal; two agents act simultaneously.
team.observation: Both see ready; inspect joint action in diagnostic view.
team.reward: Team reward R(a,b)=2*a+b; both agents receive that scalar.
team.randomness: None; model-known counterfactual replaces each agent's action by IDLE.

shaping.state: A, B, T with decisions remaining h=2 or 1.
shaping.actions: At A: DIRECT or VIA; B: FINISH or WAIT.
shaping.transitions: DIRECT->T; VIA->B; FINISH->T; WAIT stays B until horizon reaches 0 and then T.
shaping.reward: DIRECT +3, VIA 0, FINISH +4, WAIT 0. Ad-hoc bonus +5 on WAIT only.
shaping.boundary: Two-decision finite horizon terminates; Phi(T)=0, Phi(A)=2, Phi(B)=1, gamma=1.

congestion.state: One shared lane and opponent policy parameter p.
congestion.observation: Lane condition; opponent choice hidden until joint transition. Fixed known p is part of the task specification.
congestion.actions: Agent CROSS or WAIT; opponent occupies lane with probability p.
congestion.transitions: CROSS succeeds only if lane is unoccupied when blocking is enabled; WAIT always ends safely.
congestion.randomness: Seeded Bernoulli opponent action; changing p during training changes the agent's induced MDP.

rps.observation: Constant start; opponent choice revealed only after both act.
rps.actions: ROCK, PAPER, SCISSORS, or a distribution over them.
rps.transitions: Joint action leads to terminal; subsequent rounds reset.
rps.reward: Win +1, tie 0, loss -1; opponent gets negative reward.
rps.randomness: Seeded independent action draws; exact payoff matrix for acceptance.

gae.state: A two-step rollout with rewards [1,2], values [0.5,1], and endpoint value 3 if continuing.
gae.transitions: Index 0->1->endpoint; distinguish genuine terminal from truncation/cutoff.
gae.boundary: Terminal case endpoint value forced 0; truncated/cutoff case bootstraps value 3, then cuts GAE recursion across reset.

ppo.state: Frozen rollout tuples (old log probability, new log probability, advantage).
ppo.observation: Ratios and advantage per sampled action.
ppo.actions: Inspect/update a two-logit policy; positive and negative advantage examples.
ppo.transitions: No environment transition in objective exercise; later library stage uses chain.
ppo.reward: Supplied advantage, not an environment reward. Clip epsilon 0.2.
ppo.boundary: Fixed rollout batch and old policy remain unchanged across update epochs.
ppo.randomness: None in objective witnesses; local integration uses seeded chain.

labs.title: Build the interaction loop
labs.objective: Implement how an agent and environment exchange actions, observations, and rewards.
labs.browser: Step through position, action, transition, reward, and terminal flag; reset or apply a collection cap.
labs.localTask: Complete reset/step and a random-agent loop with Gymnasium signatures.
labs.misconception: The agent changes the environment state directly, or can keep stepping after an episode ends.
acceptance: Reset gives position 0 and fresh info; RIGHT,RIGHT yields observations 1,2, rewards -1,5, flags false,true, total return 4.
After terminal, step raises a clear error. Reset restores 0. LEFT from 0 returns 0 with reward -1.
A 1-step external cap on RIGHT gives terminated=false,truncated=true; the collector stops without treating state 1 as terminal.
labs.transfer: Which reset/step and info contracts must the project environment preserve?

labs.title: When an observation hides the state
labs.objective: Identify when two identical observations require different transition models.
labs.browser: Compare two histories, their constant observation, and the next reward; optionally reveal mode.
labs.localTask: Add the missing mode feature; separate task state from unrelated history.
labs.misconception: Any convenient feature vector automatically satisfies the Markov property.
acceptance: From mode 0, CLAIM gives -1; after FLIP the same broken observation 0 followed by CLAIM gives +1.
Repaired observation distinguishes modes 0 and 1; repeating CLAIM from a given full state always has the same outcome.
Finite-horizon extension adds remaining time; a full unbounded history is not required.
labs.transfer: Which project features affect future rewards or legal actions?

labs.title: Reward is not return
labs.objective: Compute return at each time index and explain discount weighting.
labs.browser: Move gamma and show each contribution in the three-reward sequence.
labs.localTask: Repair backward return accumulation and show all returns, not just the episode sum.
labs.misconception: Discounting each immediate reward once produces the trajectory return.
acceptance: Rewards [2,-1,4] produce returns [2,-1,4] at gamma=0; [2.5,1,4] at gamma=0.5; [5,3,4] at gamma=1.
The first reward is undiscounted at its own time; terminal tail contributes zero.
labs.transfer: Why is the project training return distinct from physical race time if rewards are centred?

labs.title: One Bellman backup
labs.objective: Distinguish state value, action value, policy evaluation, and optimality.
labs.browser: Inspect action branches and toggle policy probabilities and gamma.
labs.localTask: Implement expectation/optimality backups with terminal value zero and legal-action masks.
labs.misconception: A policy-average value and the best action's value are interchangeable.
acceptance: At gamma=0.5, Q(A,DIRECT)=3, Q(A,VIA)=1+0.5*4=3; a uniform policy gives V(A)=3.
At gamma=1, action values are 3 and 5, V under uniform policy is 4 and optimal value is 5.
An illegal action with stored value 99 never participates in the maximum.
labs.transfer: Why must the agent and oracle share action validity?

labs.title: Solve a tiny model exactly
labs.objective: Solve a finite known model and verify it without using its own recurrence as the oracle.
labs.browser: Animate leaves-to-root values with remaining decisions visible.
labs.localTask: Complete a time-indexed solver and independent enumeration of legal policies.
labs.misconception: Backward induction is trial-and-error training, or time need not appear in a finite-horizon value table.
acceptance: At gamma=1 with two decisions, optimal start value is 5 via B; exhaustive route returns are 3 and 5.
With one decision and reward-only horizon termination, VIA returns 1, so DIRECT wins with 3.
Terminal value is zero at all horizons; no look-ahead beyond the boundary.
labs.transfer: Which quantities does the DP oracle know that a model-free learner does not?

labs.title: What happens to the unlikely outcome?
labs.objective: Compute probability-weighted values rather than pick the modal outcome.
labs.browser: Change probability p and inspect outcome contributions and best action.
labs.localTask: Repair an expected-value backup and validate transition normalization.
labs.misconception: The most likely next state is an adequate substitute for the transition distribution.
acceptance: RISKY at p=0.25 is 0.25*10+0.75*(-2)=1, so SAFE=2 wins; at p=0.5 RISKY=4 wins.
At p=1/3 both actions have expected return 2.
Reject negative probabilities or a row summing to 1.1 rather than silently normalizing an erroneous model.
labs.transfer: How does the oracle account for possible safety-car/weather outcomes?

labs.title: Sampling a Markov chain
labs.objective: Separate an observed stochastic state from knowledge of its future realization.
labs.browser: Compare exact transition probabilities, seeded samples, and foresight decisions.
labs.localTask: Implement seeded sampling and a one-step foresight comparison.
labs.misconception: A policy with advance knowledge is a fair achievable target for a policy that only sees the current state.
acceptance: From DRY, probability of DRY after two transitions is 0.8*0.8+0.2*0.3=0.70.
One-step prediction reward from DRY is at most 0.8 without foresight and 1 with next regime revealed.
Stationary distribution is [0.6,0.4]; use a fixed sample budget and stated sampling tolerance for frequency checks, not exact counts.
labs.transfer: Explain information gap versus learning gap for the two project oracles.

labs.title: Update one Q-table cell
labs.objective: Calculate target, TD error, and the resulting table update.
labs.browser: Change alpha/gamma and next-action mask; compare true terminal with time-limit truncation.
labs.localTask: Complete masked Q-learning update and boundary handling.
labs.misconception: All collection boundaries erase bootstrap, or invalid next actions can enter the target.
acceptance: Q=2,r=1,gamma=0.5,alpha=0.25 and legal next values [4,8] give target 5,error 3,new Q=2.75.
For true terminal with same stored next values, target 1,new Q=1.75; a time-limit truncation of N retains target 5.
The masked 99 must not give target 50.5.
labs.transfer: Where do next-state action masks and terminated flags enter the project update?

labs.title: An agent that never discovers B
labs.objective: Separate behaviour exploration from greedy evaluation.
labs.browser: Inspect action probabilities and visits as epsilon changes; label sampled runs.
labs.localTask: Implement legal epsilon-greedy sampling, seeded tie-breaking, and evaluation mode.
labs.misconception: Greedy choice necessarily finds the best action, or exploration belongs only in evaluation.
acceptance: With Q=[0.6,0.1], two legal actions and epsilon=0.2, probabilities are [0.9,0.1].
With epsilon=1 and mask [true,true,false], C has probability 0 and A/B each 0.5.
Evaluation epsilon=0 selects current best action; report multi-seed training rather than require a win on one seed.
labs.transfer: What state must be reset or disabled when evaluating a trained agent?

labs.title: The action you actually take next
labs.objective: Use the executed next action for an on-policy TD target.
labs.browser: Show careful/slip sampling and contrast max-Q with the committed sampled action.
labs.localTask: Implement SARSA action commitment; clear it on reset and evaluation.
labs.misconception: SARSA can resample the next action after using a different one in its update target.
acceptance: With Q(RISK)=[6,-10], gamma=1 and r=0, max target is 6; sampled slip gives SARSA target -10.
At epsilon=0.2, the risky state's behaviour value is 0.9*6+0.1*(-10)=4.4, not 6.
A supplied slip action is executed on the next step; a reset cannot leak it into the next episode.
labs.transfer: Why does cached next-action state require episode reset in the project SARSA agent?

labs.title: When more training cannot help
labs.objective: Diagnose an encoder unable to represent two different optimal choices.
labs.browser: Move bin boundaries and compare encoded states and best actions.
labs.localTask: Repair the boundary convention and nonuniform bins; inspect resulting table size.
labs.misconception: More training can recover distinctions the observation encoder has removed.
acceptance: x=0.49 prefers LEFT and x=0.51 prefers RIGHT; one bin forces the same deterministic action for both.
Bins [0,0.5,1] distinguish these values; x=0.5 belongs to the RIGHT side and x=1 remains in the final valid bin.
Doubling every axis across d dimensions multiplies dense table entries by 2^d.
labs.transfer: Can the project's bins distinguish critical neighbouring pit decisions?

labs.title: From table entries to a function
labs.objective: Follow tensors through forward pass, scalar loss, gradients, and an optimizer step.
labs.browser: Inspect a one-input/two-output linear network before introducing hidden layers.
labs.localTask: Implement prediction/MSE/update; then fit Q labels on a small held-out split.
labs.misconception: Changing predicted Q-values is the same operation as choosing an action.
acceptance: At x=0.25 with zero weights/biases, outputs [0,0], target [0.25,0.75], mean squared error is 0.3125.
Bias gradient for that mean loss is [-0.25,-0.75]; weight gradient is [-0.0625,-0.1875].
Batch B has output shape (B,2), finite gradients, and a held-out error metric; warm-up is supervised learning, not DQN training.
labs.transfer: What shape must the project's network return for every observation batch?

labs.title: A target that changes under your feet
labs.objective: Distinguish replay decorrelation, sample reuse, target lag, and target detachment.
labs.browser: Inspect buffer order and online/target snapshots; replay recorded training only with provenance.
labs.localTask: Implement FIFO replay, detached target outputs, scheduled copies, and small ablations.
labs.misconception: A second variable pointing to the online network is an independent frozen target.
acceptance: Online outputs change from [1,2] to [3,4] while target stays [1,2] until explicit synchronization.
Backpropagation produces online gradients but no target gradients.
Capacity 4 after inserting transition IDs 0..5 contains 2,3,4,5; each has uniform sampling probability 0.25.
labs.transfer: How do you prove the target is an independent snapshot rather than an alias?

labs.title: Selection, evaluation, and advantage
labs.objective: Separate online action selection from target evaluation and centre advantages.
labs.browser: Show the selected legal action and value/advantage contributions.
labs.localTask: Implement masked Double DQN targets and dueling aggregation; teach Double DQN as an extension because its linked reading page is absent.
labs.misconception: Double DQN takes the target network maximum; dueling advantages have a unique absolute level.
acceptance: Online=[5,4,100],target=[1,7,99],mask=[true,true,false],r=1,gamma=0.5: Double DQN target=1.5; masked vanilla DQN target=4.5.
V=2,A=[1,3] gives Q=[1,3]; adding 10 to both advantages leaves Q unchanged.
Terminal target is 1; invalid action 2 is never selected even though it has the largest online value.
labs.transfer: Which network chooses and which evaluates the next action in the project agent?

labs.title: Why is this transition sampled so often?
labs.objective: Distinguish raw priority, probability, and importance weight.
labs.browser: Adjust alpha/beta and show exact probabilities and sampled counts.
labs.localTask: Implement priority updates and weighted loss; supply missing PER theory in the lab.
labs.misconception: Priority exponentiation and importance weighting are the same operation.
acceptance: Priorities [1,4,9] with alpha=0.5 give weights [1,2,3] and probabilities [1/6,1/3,1/2].
For N=3,beta=1, unnormalized importance weights are [2,1,2/3]; max-normalized weights [1,0.5,1/3].
Adding a new item with max raw priority 9 gives transformed priority 3 once, not sqrt(3); alpha=0 gives uniform probabilities.
labs.transfer: Does the project buffer store raw or transformed priorities, and where is alpha applied?

labs.title: One reward, two contributors
labs.objective: Understand why identical team rewards need not mean identical contributions.
labs.browser: Inspect joint actions and optional model-known counterfactuals.
labs.localTask: Implement simultaneous joint actions and shared rewards; enumerate contributions.
labs.misconception: A shared scalar reward identifies how much each agent caused the outcome.
acceptance: Joint HELP,HELP yields reward 3 to both agents, but IDLE counterfactual differences are 2 for agent A and 1 for B.
HELP,IDLE gives 2; IDLE,HELP gives 1; IDLE,IDLE gives 0.
Explain that counterfactual rewards require the supplied model, not free information available in all environments.
labs.transfer: What tradeoff appears when the project objective changes from elapsed time to relative position?

labs.title: A reward bonus changes the goal
labs.objective: Preserve the base objective while adding a potential difference.
labs.browser: Enumerate routes and compare base, arbitrary, and potential-shaped totals.
labs.localTask: Implement shaping with task discount and zero terminal potential; compare all tiny policies.
labs.misconception: Any dense reward bonus preserves the original optimal policy.
acceptance: Unshaped DIRECT=3,VIA+FINISH=4,VIA+WAIT=0; a +5 bonus on WAIT gives 3,4,5 and makes failing to finish optimal.
With Phi(A)=2,Phi(B)=1,Phi(T)=0,gamma=1, shaped route returns are 1,2,-2: every route shifts by -2.
Nonzero terminal potentials can change rankings when endpoints differ; verify finite-horizon telescoping including the boundary term.
labs.transfer: What terminal handling does the project's potential function need?

labs.title: The environment changes when others act
labs.objective: Distinguish missing interaction mechanics from a changing opponent distribution.
labs.browser: Toggle blocking separately from p; inspect exact expected reward and sampled outcomes.
labs.localTask: Implement the shared-lane effect and controlled changes of opponent policy.
labs.misconception: An opponent affects learning even when its actions never affect dynamics.
acceptance: With blocking on, CROSS expected reward is 1-2p: p=0.2 gives 0.6; p=0.8 gives -0.6, so WAIT wins.
With blocking off, CROSS always gives 1 regardless of p; an unused collision function cannot change outcomes.
Holding p fixed gives stationary induced transitions; changing p changes them even for the same observed agent action.
labs.transfer: How can you verify overtaking/traffic functions actually affect the project transition?

labs.title: Best against whom?
planSections: Background: Why Self-Play Needs Special Handling
labs.objective: Distinguish a best response to one opponent from a robust mixed strategy.
labs.browser: Explore the exact payoff matrix and mixed distributions.
labs.localTask: Build fixed-opponent updates and exact payoff evaluation; introduce distribution/vector math beside it.
labs.misconception: Beating a fixed opponent proves convergence to a game equilibrium.
acceptance: Against pure ROCK, PAPER scores +1; PAPER against SCISSORS scores -1.
Uniform [1/3,1/3,1/3] has expected payoff 0 against each pure opponent.
Against mixture [0.5,0.25,0.25], PAPER expected payoff is 0.5-0.25=0.25.
labs.transfer: Why should project evaluation cover multiple opponent styles?

labs.title: Winning today, forgetting yesterday
labs.objective: Keep independent historical snapshots and evaluate opponent coverage.
labs.browser: Show payoff matrices and normalized pool-sampling weights.
labs.localTask: Implement immutable policy copies, bounded pool, seeded sampling, and held-out evaluations.
labs.misconception: A list of references to a changing learner is a history of independent checkpoints.
acceptance: Snapshot [0.2,0.3,0.5] stays unchanged after learner becomes [1,0,0].
Pool weights [1,2,3] normalize to [1/6,1/3,1/2]; a genuinely random initial policy samples all three actions.
PAPER scores +1 against ROCK but -1 against held-out SCISSORS; latest-opponent wins alone do not demonstrate overall improvement.
labs.transfer: How is pool initialization different from greedy action selection with random weights?

labs.title: An impressive result with a weak comparison
labs.objective: Audit pairings, exploration mode, null comparisons, and multi-agent lifecycle.
labs.browser: Inspect seed/score rows and compare marginals with paired differences.
labs.localTask: Repair evaluation scheduling and add a small AEC/parallel lifecycle stage using the same one-round game.
labs.misconception: Using the same master seed alone guarantees identical per-scenario evaluation pairings.
acceptance: Scenario scores A=[2,8],B=[1,7] give paired differences [1,1]; reversed B pairing gives [-5,7] with same mean but misleading spread.
A parallel one-round game consumes both live-agent actions once and then agents is empty; AEC dead-agent cleanup uses the selected agent's termination flag.
A shuffled-pairing null result is not evidence of no learning by itself; inspect the defined statistic and opponent coverage.
labs.transfer: What must be held fixed in the project's paired evaluation?

labs.title: Learn probabilities directly
labs.objective: Translate a log-probability gradient into a sampled policy update.
labs.browser: Change two logits, pick an explicit sample, and inspect probabilities before/after.
labs.localTask: Implement REINFORCE loss and explain gradient ascent versus loss descent.
labs.misconception: A positive return should lower the sampled action's log probability under loss minimization.
acceptance: Logits [0,0], sampled action A,return 2: loss gradient [-1,1]; SGD rate 0.1 produces logits [0.1,-0.1].
New A probability is approximately 0.549834; a negative return reverses the gradient.
Positive sampled return increases that sampled action even if it is suboptimal on average; distinguish one sample from expected improvement.
labs.transfer: How is the PPO acting policy different from the project Q-value argmax policy?

labs.title: Better than the baseline
labs.objective: Subtract a valid action-independent baseline and separate actor/critic gradients.
labs.browser: Compare explicit returns with a frozen state-only baseline.
labs.localTask: Implement baseline, critic loss, and actor advantage detachment.
labs.misconception: Any baseline, including one depending on sampled action, leaves the policy gradient unbiased.
acceptance: Returns 8 and 2 with baseline 5 give advantages +3 and -3.
At uniform policy, E[score*b]=0 for state-only b=5; with b(A)=1,b(B)=0 expected baseline score is [0.25,-0.25], not zero.
Actor backward does not update critic through the detached advantage; critic updates separately. Compare variance rather than assume any baseline reduces it.
labs.transfer: Which learned value head helps estimate PPO's training signal?

labs.title: Carry the right signal backward
labs.objective: Compute GAE without mixing true terminals, time limits, and rollout cutoffs.
labs.browser: Walk residuals backward with gamma=0.9 and lambda controls.
labs.localTask: Implement bootstrap mask and separate trace-continuation mask.
labs.misconception: Lambda 1 always equals a nonbootstrapped Monte Carlo return, even on a truncated rollout.
acceptance: Terminal endpoint: residuals [1.4,1]; lambda=0 gives [1.4,1], lambda=1 gives [2.3,1].
Continuing endpoint V=3: residuals [1.4,3.7]; lambda=1 gives [4.73,3.7], lambda=0.5 gives [3.065,3.7].
Use the final observation for truncation bootstrap, not the auto-reset observation; cut recursion across an episode reset.
labs.transfer: Which PPO configuration and rollout boundaries control the advantage estimate?

labs.title: Clipping an incentive, not a probability
labs.objective: Implement the clipped surrogate and recognize its limits; inspect library integration separately.
labs.browser: Move ratio and advantage sign; label clipped versus unclipped branches and KL diagnostic.
labs.localTask: Implement negative-mean surrogate loss; freeze old log probabilities; stage optional Windows factory and experience-budget checks.
labs.misconception: PPO clip epsilon is a hard bound on every action probability ratio.
acceptance: Updating new logits leaves old log probabilities unchanged; negative mean objective is the loss being minimized.

Eight environments * 128 vector steps yields 1024 transitions; compare with 1024 single-environment steps. Demonstrate actual spawn serialization behaviour for installed library versions instead of assuming every lambda fails.
labs.transfer: What makes DQN/PPO budgets and evaluation conditions comparable?
